title: Locality of derived finite-coefficient coinduction
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Assume that $B$, as an $A$-module, admits an augmented exact resolution $P^\bullet\to B[0]$ with $P^i=0$ for $i>0$ and each $P^i$ a finite direct sum of copies of $A$. Let $X$ be a scheme, and use constant coefficient sheaves and small etale bounded-below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ define derived coinduction $C_X(K)\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ by the complex $\mathcal Hom_A(B_X,I^\bullet)$ for a bounded-below injective representative $I^\bullet$ of $K$, with $(b h)(b')=h(bb')$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. It is right adjoint to exact restriction of scalars. If $K\in D^{\geq a}$, then $C_X(K)\in D^{\geq a}$.

For every scheme morphism $g:Y\to X$ there is a natural $B$-linear isomorphism
$$g^*C_X(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_Y(g^*K),$$
where inverse image means the exact constant-coefficient functor [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. For every closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], with $i^!$ the right derived functor of the supported kernel [def-pur-etale-supported-kernel], there is a natural $B$-linear isomorphism
$$i_B^!C_X(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_Z(i_A^!K).$$
The latter is the right-adjoint comparison induced by commutation of restriction of scalars with closed direct image, and respects the closed counits. These comparisons commute with compositions. Consequently, if $x\in X$ and $R\Gamma_xK$ denotes closed extraordinary restriction after localization at $x$, they induce
$$c_x:R\Gamma_xC_X(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)}(R\Gamma_xK),$$
also after taking a geometric fibre [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-geometric-point]. For a locally free rank-one $A_X$-module $L$ (one locally isomorphic to $A_X$) and $L_B=B_X\otimes_{A_X}L$, there is a natural isomorphism $C_X(K\otimes_A L)\cong C_X(K)\otimes_B L_B$; all these comparisons respect cohomological shifts. No constructibility, finite Tor amplitude of $K$, or finite projective dimension of $B$ over $A$ is required.

proof.text:
Write $U_X$ for restriction from $B_X$-modules to $A_X$-modules and $H_X(F)=\mathcal Hom_A(B_X,F)$ with the indicated $B$-action. Restriction is exact: it leaves the underlying abelian sheaf, sectionwise kernels, and sheafified cokernels unchanged. The sheaf Hom definition gives mutually inverse maps
$$\operatorname{Hom}_A(U_XM,F)\longleftrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_B(M,H_XF),\quad t\mapsto(m\mapsto[b\mapsto t(bm)]),\quad s\mapsto(m\mapsto s(m)(1)).$$
These formulas commute with restriction on the localized sites, are linear, and are inverse since $s(bm)(1)=(bs(m))(1)=s(m)(b)$. Thus $U_X\dashv H_X$, with evaluation at $1$ as counit. By the exact-left-adjoint lemma $H_X$ sends injectives to injectives.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 6.2.1.1, printed p. 294; explicit agent expansion of supported-cohomology commutation

proof.text:
There are enough injective module sheaves. Choose a bounded-below injective representative $I$ of $K$; when $K\in D^{\geq a}$ choose $I^q=0$ for $q<a$. The previous step makes $H_X(I)$ a bounded-below complex of injective $B$-sheaves, with the same lower bound. The termwise homotopy adjunction and the K-injective computation of derived morphisms give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A_X)}(U_XM,K)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A_X)}(U_XM,I)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(B_X)}(M,H_XI)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B_X)}(M,QH_XI).$$
Here $M$ denotes any bounded-below complex representing the input. This proves the derived adjunction. A quasi-isomorphism between injective representatives is a homotopy equivalence; the additive functor $H_X$ preserves its homotopies. Consequently the construction is independent of representatives, with the canonical comparisons and evaluation counit. It is $C_X$, and the termwise lower bound proves the asserted $D^{\geq a}$ bound.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 6.2.1.1, printed p. 294; explicit agent expansion of supported-cohomology commutation

proof.text:
Apply the exact constant-module-sheaf functor to $P\to B[0]$, so $P_X\to B_X[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. For a bounded-below representative $N$ of $K$, the finite-free Hom model computes the underlying $A$-object of $C_X(K)$ by
$$T_X(N)=\mathcal Hom_A^\bullet(P_X,N),\qquad T_X(N)^n=\bigoplus_{a-n\leq p\leq0}\mathcal Hom_A(P_X^p,N^{p+n})$$
if $N^q=0$ for $q<a$. This identification is the canonical one induced by the augmentation and injective comparison, by invariance of derived internal Hom. The differential is $d_Nf-(-1)^nf d_P$. In particular every diagonal is finite, even though $P$ can extend indefinitely to the left. We use $T_X$ only after forgetting to $A$; we do not put a fictitious strict $B$-action on $P$.

For $g:Y\to X$, exact constant-coefficient inverse image commutes with restriction of scalars. Define $\beta_g:g_B^*C_XK\to C_Yg_A^*K$ as the $U_Y\dashv C_Y$ adjunct of $g_A^*\varepsilon_K:U_Yg_B^*C_XK=g_A^*U_XC_XK\to g_A^*K$. This defines an actual $B$-linear derived morphism. Its scalar restriction is the usual sheaf-Hom pullback comparison: before deriving, both are adjoint to $(h,b)\mapsto h(b)$, and deriving uses the same injective comparison and augmentation as Step 3. Since $P^p=A^{r_p}$ with $r_p$ finite, evaluation on its basis identifies each term $\mathcal Hom_A(P_X^p,N^q)$ with $N^{q\,\oplus r_p}$. In these coordinates the pullback comparison is the canonical finite-sum isomorphism. It commutes with $d_N$ by functoriality and with $d_P$ because that differential is a matrix of constant $A$-scalars. The finite-diagonal formula therefore makes $U_Y\beta_g$ an isomorphism of derived $A$-objects. Restriction reflects isomorphisms: a cone is acyclic exactly when its underlying abelian sheaf cohomology vanishes. Thus $\beta_g$ is an isomorphism over $B$.

proof.text: For a closed immersion $i$, the supported-kernel adjunction on abelian sheaves extends to sheaves of modules over either constant ring: all kernel and inverse-image maps carry scalar actions; its bijection restricts to linear maps since applying it to the equation $t\circ r=r\circ t$ gives exactly that equation on the other side. Exactness of $i_*$ on module sheaves follows from exactness on the underlying abelian sheaves. Hence $i_*\dashv i_0^!$ and $i_0^!$ preserves injectives. Apply the bounded-below injective and homotopy-category calculation of Step 2 to this adjunction. It identifies $i_*\dashv Ri_0^!=i^!$ on $D^+$, with the derived supported-kernel counit. This justifies the closed adjunction used below without assuming a constructible exceptional-functor package.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 6.2.1.1, printed p. 294; explicit agent expansion of supported-cohomology commutation

proof.text:
Restriction of scalars commutes with closed direct image: on an etale $V\to X$, both $U_Xi_{*,B}M$ and $i_{*,A}U_ZM$ have sections $M(V\times_XZ)$ and the same $A$-action. The composite-adjunction theorem identifies the right adjoints of this common functor:
$$i_B^!C_X\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ C_Zi_A^!.$$
Concretely, for $M\in D^+(Z,B)$ their representing Hom functors are identified by
$$\operatorname{Hom}_B(M,i_B^!C_XK)=\operatorname{Hom}_A(U_Xi_{*,B}M,K)=\operatorname{Hom}_A(i_{*,A}U_ZM,K)=\operatorname{Hom}_B(M,C_Zi_A^!K).$$
The comparison is therefore $B$-linear and preserves the pasted evaluation and closed counits, as the composite-adjunction theorem states. In particular its normalization is the one in the item, not an arbitrary isomorphism between the two objects.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 6.2.1.1, printed p. 294; explicit agent expansion of supported-cohomology commutation

proof.text: For composable inverse images $h^*,g^*$ the mate of $h^*\beta_g$ followed by $\beta_h$ is the pullback of the single evaluation counit, by the mate-pasting identity; this is also the mate defining $\beta_{gh}$. Identity pullback gives the identity comparison. Closed comparisons compose by the same pasting identity applied to the commutative squares $Ui_*=i_*U$; their pasted counits are exactly those of the composite closed adjunction. Thus the two comparisons have the stated composition compatibilities. This verifies equality of comparison morphisms in the coefficient category itself.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 6.2.1.1, printed p. 294; explicit agent expansion of supported-cohomology commutation

proof.text:
Let $l_x:\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}\to X$ and $s_x:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}$ be localization and the closed point. By the meaning of $R\Gamma_x$ in the statement, it is $s_x^!l_x^*$. Compose the established comparisons in that order:
$$s_{x,B}^!l_x^*C_XK\xrightarrow{s_x^!\beta_{l_x}}s_{x,B}^!C_{X_x}l_x^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{\kappa(x)}s_{x,A}^!l_x^*K.$$
This is $c_x$. For a geometric point $e:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ apply $e^*$ and then $\beta_e$. This proves the geometric-fibre clause as well. No base-change theorem for extraordinary inverse image is used here: these are the successive operations that define this costalk.

proof.text:
Put $L^\vee=\mathcal Hom_A(L,A_X)$. Locally $L=A_X$, so evaluation gives $L\otimes_AL^\vee=A_X$; tensoring with $L$ and with $L^\vee$ are inverse exact functors, as can be checked in these local coordinates. Being an exact equivalence, tensoring with $L$ preserves injectives (apply the exact-left-adjoint lemma to its inverse). For injective $I^q$ the map
$$\mathcal Hom_A(B_X,I^q)\otimes_BL_B\longrightarrow\mathcal Hom_A(B_X,I^q\otimes_AL),\quad h\otimes(b\otimes l)\longmapsto[b'\mapsto h(bb')\otimes l]$$
is balanced and $B$-linear. It is an isomorphism locally where $L=A_X$, hence globally, and commutes with $d_I$. Both sides consequently compute the claimed derived objects using $I$ and $I\otimes L$. Inverting this map gives the direction displayed in the statement. All the maps used above arise from additive functors, degree-zero evaluation, the signed Hom differential, and pasted units and counits; shifting a representative gives those same maps with the usual cochain shift signs. They therefore respect cohomological shifts. Only the lower bound on $K$ and finiteness of each $P^p$ were used; no bound on the length of $P$, constructibility, or Tor amplitude entered.
